newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha lower, extra LSWR seen allocated.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha lower, extra LSWR seen allocated.

text.p: Naphtha prices declined for the first time in five business days on Friday, dragged down by a sharp loss in overnight crude prices, traders said.
In low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading, Indonesia was rumoured to have allocated additional cargoes for July loading.
The exact volume was unclear, but traders said the extra allotment was likely to be a "few hundred thousand" barrels.

They said the additional allocation was unlikely to put a downward pressure on the regional LSWR market as the combined volume of the initial and additional allocation would be still far smaller than initial allotments for preceding months.
Pertamina initially allocated 2.3 million barrels of LSWR for July, compared with 3.1 million barrels for June, and 3.7 to 3.9 million for May.
LSWR trading remained largely quiet amid a lack of spot availability, traders added.
Levels for July cargoes were notionally quoted at $1.00 to $1.20 per barrel over the Pertamina formula.
Asia's benchmark forward contract open-spec naphtha was assessed at $199.00/200.00 per tonne for first-half September delivery, down from Thursday's $201.75/202.75.
